Rarity.maps_to: Potion.rarity = 'event' (potions.py:352), read by shop.MerchantPotionEntry pricing and by potion_pools.POTION_POOL's rarity bucket (potion_pools.py:38-65)
Rarity.rationale: EXECUTED, not asserted: `py audit/tools/potion_probes.py sweep-attrs` extracts PotionRarity from every C# model and diffs it against the sim class attribute over all 51 units and reports 0 mismatches. Rarity is observable in the sim (it sets the shop price and the reward-roll bucket), so this is a behavioural verdict rather than a field copy. Event rarity keeps it out of the reward/shop pool, which potions.py:353 records as in_reward_pool = False and potion_pools.POTION_POOL records by omission; it is granted only by the ported Drowning Beacon event (events/drowning_beacon.py:28). NOTE a roster fact for the report: this is the tier's only name override -- the sim id `glowwater` does not derive GlowwaterPotion.cs, so audit/tools/name_overrides.json carries `potion/glowwater`.

Usage.maps_to: no explicit attribute; the sim's only potion-use entry point is CombatState.use_potion (combat.py:583-616), which cannot be reached outside a combat
Usage.rationale: PotionUsage.CombatOnly means the game's Use button is live only during a fight. The sim reaches that by construction: `py audit/tools/potion_probes.py sweep-usage` finds exactly one `def use_potion` in sts2_rl/, on CombatState, and the conformance driver only dispatches the recording's UsePotion command inside a live fight (conformance/combat_driver.py:16,263-289). The absence of a `usage` attribute is therefore not a dropped guard for this unit -- but it IS a real gap for the four AnyTime potions, which is where the divergence is filed (blood_potion, entropic_brew, foul_potion, fruit_juice).

TargetType.maps_to: no attribute -- `targeted` stays False, so CombatState.use_potion passes target=None (combat.py:608) and the potion applies to ctx.player (potions.py:356-360)
TargetType.rationale: TargetType.Self in a single-player run always resolves to the owner: PotionModel.EnqueueManualUse defaults `target` to `Owner.Creature` when it is a valid target (PotionModel.cs:240-243) and IsValidTarget's Self/AnyPlayer arms accept exactly that creature (PotionModel.cs:280-287). The multiplayer half -- AnyPlayer letting you throw the potion at an ally, and CanThrowAtAlly (PotionModel.cs:381-388) gating it on `RunState.Players.Count > 1` -- is out of scope by the shared contract and noted in maps_to rather than verdicted as a divergence.

ExtraHoverTips.maps_to: no counterpart; the sim has no hover-tip surface
ExtraHoverTips.rationale: ExtraHoverTips / HoverTipFactory / PotionModel.HoverTip are the potion tooltip's keyword lines. Waived under the shared contract's presentation exclusion, not under any unreachability claim.

OnUse (protected override, GlowwaterPoti.rationale: Snapshot the hand, exhaust every card in it, then draw 10. C# takes the snapshot explicitly (`PileType.Hand.GetPile(Owner).Cards.ToList()`, GlowwaterPotion.cs:31) because the loop mutates the pile it reads; potions.py:358 does the same with `list(ctx.player.hand)`. Both exhaust through the ordinary verb (CardCmd.Exhaust vs ExhaustCmd.exhaust, cmds.py:371-384) so on_card_exhausted fires per card in hand order, and both draw AFTER the whole hand is gone -- which matters, since drawing first would exhaust the newly drawn cards.

guards.what: N1: no MinSelect question here -- Glowwater exhausts the WHOLE hand unconditionally
guards.rationale: Deliberately contrasted with potion/ashwater, whose LIVE G1 is that the sim always exhausts everything. Here that IS the rule: GlowwaterPotion.cs:31-35 iterates the hand with no CardSelectCmd at all, so 'exhaust the whole hand' is correct and the sim's unconditional loop is faithful. PROMPT.md bug class 29 in reverse -- two hand-exhausting potions where copying either verdict across would have been wrong.

guards.what: N2: the 10-card draw is hand-size capped on both sides, and the hand is empty when it starts
guards.rationale: The sim's MAX_HAND_SIZE is 10 (player.py:56) and _draw stops at it (player.py:278-279), so a 10-card draw into an empty hand is exactly at the cap and nothing is lost -- which is presumably why the number is 10. The draw also stops when both piles run dry on both sides (player.py:282-289 vs CardPileCmd.Draw's ShuffleIfNecessary). Recorded because 10 is the largest draw in the tier and an off-by-one at the cap would be invisible in every other potion.

guards.what: W4: PotionModel.cs:324-331 brackets OnUse in BeginCardOrPotionEffect/EndCardOrPotionEffect and the sim has no re-entrancy depth counter
guards.issue: CombatManager.cs:889's `!IsExecutingCardOrPotionEffect(player)` is what stops a nested effect from triggering the empty-hand check early, and PotionModel.cs:324-331 is what puts a potion inside that bracket. The sim has no counterpart anywhere. DORMANT for the same reason audit/records/relic/unceasing_top.json G2 is dormant -- the ported cards that auto-play another card mid-resolution (cards/cascade.py:58, cards/colorless_skills.py:117) do not touch the draw pile between the inner and outer ends -- but recorded separately because the OUTER frame here is a potion, so a fix that brackets only card plays would leave this half open. What would make it live: any ported potion or card that empties the hand and then moves the draw pile from inside a nested auto-play.
